newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mostly up, seen catching cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mostly up, seen catching cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mostly higher Monday as futures contracts caught up with strong physical power prices ahead of the cold winter months, industry sources said.
"It seemed as though it was only a matter of time before we had another real run up in futures prices, and this seems to be part of that," said one futures broker.

The futures prices were catching up with some of the physicals values being offered by large utilities, including the Bonneville Power Administration which was offering Tuesday peak power at $27.75 per megawatt hour (MWh), the sources said.
Stronger natural gas futures prices and below-normal temperatures in the Northwest were also seen putting upward pressure on power futures.
However, strong resistance was seen for December California Oregon Border (COB) at $26.00, the sources said.
December COB futures ended up 41 cents at $25.91 per MWh after hitting a new contract high of $26.25, while January COB settled down two cents at $23.00 after trade as high as $23.65 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds were mosly down 15 cents.
December Palo Verde (PV) closed up 41 cents at $24.00 after trade as high as $24.25, while January PV ended up 33 cents at $21.33 after trade as high as $21.50 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds were mostly up between 25 and 80 cents.
April, August and September PV futures all hit new contract highs.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 160 COB and 33 PV contracts traded Monday.
